Certainly, here are some healthy and easy dinner ideas for the week:

1. Sheet Pan Baked Salmon: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat. Place the salmon fillets on the sheet and season with lemon zest, salt, black pepper, and minced garlic. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the salmon and add sliced herbs like dill, parsley, or thyme, if desired. Toss cherry tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and black pepper, and add them to the sheet pan around the salmon. Roast in the oven for 12-15 minutes or until the salmon is cooked through and flakes easily.

2. Turkey Chili: In a large pot or Dutch oven, sauté diced onions and bell peppers with ground turkey over medium heat until browned. Add chili powder, cumin, minced garlic, and a can of diced tomatoes (optional). Bring the mixture to a simmer and let cook for 10-15 minutes. Add canned kidney beans (drained and rinsed), salt, and black pepper.

3. Mason Jar Salads: Mason jar salads are a great option for a healthy and easy dinner that allows for a customizable mix of ingredients. Start by layering your choice of leafy greens, beans (such as chickpeas or black beans), hard vegetables (such as carrots, cucumbers, or broccoli), and toppings (such as nuts, seeds, dried fruits, or cheese). Keep dressings separate and stir before serving.

4. One-Pan Stuffed Sweet Potatoes: Roast sweet potatoes (any variety) until tender, then cut them in half lengthwise and fluff them up with fork. Brush with olive oil and sprinkle with salt and black pepper. Fill each sweet potato half with a mixture of cooked quinoa, sautéed spinach or kale, and chopped walnuts or pecans. You can also add sliced chicken breast or canned black beans for extra protein.

5. Veggie Frittata Muffins: In a mixing bowl, whisk together eggs, salt, and black pepper. Add grated veggies such as zucchini, bell peppers, and red onion, as well as shredded cheese (optional). Spray a muffin tin with oil or coat with parchment paper. Divide the mixture evenly among the muffin cups and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20-25 minutes, or until set.

6. Slow Cooker Whole Grain Bowls: In a slow cooker, combine washed quinoa, black beans (if using dried, soak first), vegetable broth, diced tomatoes, onion powder, garlic powder, and salt. Cook on high for 2-3 hours. Let cool, then divide the cooked grain mixture into portions and top with your favorite toppings, such as sliced avocado, chopped fresh cilantro, and a squeeze of lime.

7. Grilled Chicken Fajita Bowls: Marinate chicken breasts in fajita seasoning, olive oil, and lime juice for at least 30 minutes. Preheat grill or a grill pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken until fully cooked, then let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing. Serve the sliced chicken over a bed of lettuce or brown rice, topped with your favorite fajita veggies (such as sautéed onions, bell peppers, and mushrooms) and avocado. Add salsa, sour cream (optional), and extra lime wedges if desired.

8. Sheet Pan Chicken Fajitas: Follow a similar method to the grilled chicken fajitas (above), but bake in a sheet pan at 400°F (200°C) for 15-20 minutes. Use a sheet pan liner or silicone mat and arrange the chicken over one side, then add sliced bell peppers, onions, and chili powder. You can also add other desired seasonings such as cumin, paprika, or garlic powder. Serve with warm tortillas and toppings such as sliced avocado, cilantro, and lime wedges.

9. Baked Honey Mustard Salmon: In a mixing bowl, whisk together Dijon mustard, olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper. Add honey and mix well. Transfer the mixture to a baking dish large enough to accommodate the salmon fillets (you can bake multiple fillets at a time) and spread the honey mustard mixture evenly over the salmon. Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 12-15 minutes or until the salmon is cooked through.

10. One-Pot Chicken and Veggies: In a large pot, brown sliced chicken with olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper. Add chopped vegetables of your choice, such as broccoli, cauliflower, carrots, and sweet potatoes. If desired, drizzle a tablespoon of balsamic vinegar over the vegetables. Pour in enough chicken broth to cover the chicken and vegetables, then bring to a boil. Reduce heat and let simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the chicken and vegetables are tender.

11. Turkey and Vegetable Stir-Fry: In a wok or a large skillet, heat some oil over medium-high heat. Add minced garlic, ginger, and red bell pepper. Add ground turkey and cook until browned. Push the ingredients to the sides and add sliced vegetables such as broccoli, carrots, onions, and bean sprouts. Season with soy sauce and black pepper, and toss everything together until well combined and heated through. Serve hot.

Popcorn is a snack made from popping corn kernels, which do not fall under traditional foods as they are not cooked dishes. Therefore, I will provide a cooking tip to enhance the flavor of a popular popcorn-inspired dish:

Flavored popcorn is a delicious and customizable snack that can be easily enhanced in flavor. Here are a few tips to improve the taste of flavored popcorn:

1. Use the right type of popcorn: Different varieties of popcorn kernels may have slightly different natural flavors. Look for popcorn kernels labeled as "popping corn," "entertainment popcorn," or "movie popcorn" which are typically varieties of field corn that have a larger, sweeter kernel size, as they tend to result in a better-tasting popcorn.

2. Season at the right time: Toss your freshly popped popcorn with desired seasonings while the popcorn is still hot. This ensures that the seasonings adhere well to the kernels and infuse the popcorn with flavor. However, be careful not to overseason the popcorn, as the heat from the popping process can intensify the saltiness or spiciness of some seasonings.

3. Customize the seasoning blend: To customize the flavor of your flavored popcorn, try experimenting with different seasoning combinations. Here are some ideas:

- Sweet and Salty: Toss hot popcorn with a mix of brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and a pinch of salt for a sweet and savory snack.
- Classic Movie Theater: Give your popcorn a classic movie theater taste by seasoning it with butter-flavored popcorn salt, garlic powder, and parsley.
- Cheesy: Add a cheesy flavor to your popcorn by tossing it with a melted butter or coconut oil mixture and a tablespoon of nutritional yeast. You can also use grated Parmesan or Cheddar cheese and toss with garlic powder and Italian seasonings.
- Spicy: For a spicy kick, mix your popcorn with chili powder, cayenne pepper, or smoked paprika, depending on your preference for heat level. You can balance the heat with a sprinkle of cinnamon and a pinch of salt.

Remember, these tips are for flavored popcorn, which is not cooked kernels and thus cannot spoil. However, be mindful of over-seasoning to avoid overpowering the natural taste of the popcorn. Enjoy!

Beschreiben Sie in Ihren eigenen Worten, wie Sie das jeweilige Gericht zubereiten. Notieren Sie die Zutaten, die Sie benötigen, und die Schritte, die Sie zur Zubereitung unternehmen werden.

Zähe Chocolate Chip Cookies
output_1:
Um zähe Chocolate Chip Cookies zu backen, benötigen Sie folgende Zutaten:

- 225 g weiche Butter
- 200 g brauner Zucker
- 100 g weißer Zucker
- 2 Teelöffel Vanilleextrakt
- 2 große Eier
- 300 g Mehl
- 1/2 Teelöffel Backpulver
- 1/2 Teelöffel Salz
- 200 g Schokoladenstückchen (Chocolate Chips)

Hier sind die Schritte zur Zubereitung:

1. **Vorbereitung:** Heizen Sie Ihren Ofen auf 175°C vor und legen Sie Backpapier auf ein oder zwei Backbleche.

2. **Butter und Zucker mischen:** In einer großen Schüssel die weiche Butter mit dem braunen Zucker und dem weißen Zucker cremig rühren. Dies kann mit einem Handmixer oder einer Küchenmaschine erfolgen.

3. **Eier und Vanille hinzufügen:** Fügen Sie die Eier und den Vanilleextrakt zur Butter-Zucker-Mischung hinzu und rühren Sie alles gut durch, bis eine gleichmäßige Masse entsteht.

4. **Trockene Zutaten mischen:** In einer separaten Schüssel das Mehl mit dem Backpulver und dem Salz vermischen.

5. **Kombinieren:** Fügen Sie die trockenen Zutaten nach und nach zu der feuchten Mischung hinzu und rühren Sie weiter, bis ein gleichmäßiger Teig entsteht.

6. **Chocolate Chips hinzufügen:** Zum Schluss die Schokoladenstückchen unterheben und sicherstellen, dass sie gleichmäßig im Teig verteilt sind.

### Zutaten:
- 200 g dunkle Schokolade (vegan)
- 1 reife Avocado
- 240 ml Kokosmilch (vollfett)
- 3-4 EL Ahornsirup (je nach Geschmack)
- 1 TL Vanilleextrakt
- Eine Prise Salz

### Zubereitung:

1. **Schokolade schmelzen**: Brechen Sie die dunkle Schokolade in kleine Stücke und schmelzen Sie sie vorsichtig über einem Wasserbad oder in der Mikrowelle. Achten Sie darauf, dass die Schokolade nicht verbrennt. Lassen Sie die geschmolzene Schokolade etwas abkühlen.

2. **Avocado vorbereiten**: Halbieren Sie die Avocado, entfernen Sie den Kern und löffeln Sie das Fruchtfleisch heraus.

3. **Mousse anrühren**: Geben Sie das Avocadofleisch, die leicht abgekühlte geschmolzene Schokolade, Kokosmilch, Ahornsirup, Vanilleextrakt und eine Prise Salz in einen Mixer oder eine Küchenmaschine. Mixen Sie alles auf hoher Stufe, bis die Mischung glatt und cremig ist. Probieren Sie die Mousse und fügen Sie bei Bedarf mehr Ahornsirup hinzu.

4. **Kühlen**: Verteilen Sie die Mousse in kleine Dessertschalen oder ein großes Gefäß und stellen Sie sie für mindestens 2 Stunden in den Kühlschrank, damit sie fest wird.

instruction:
Löse diese Gleichung.

x^3 - 4x^2 + 6x - 24 = 0
output_1:
Um die Gleichung \( x^3 - 4x^2 + 6x - 24 = 0 \) zu lösen, können wir zunächst versuchen, einfache Werte für \( x \) einzusetzen, um zu sehen, ob diese die Gleichung erfüllen. Wir suchen also nach Werten von \( x \), die die Gleichung zu Null machen.

1. **Einsetzen einfacher Werte:**
   - Setze \( x = 1 \):
     \[
     1^3 - 4 \cdot 1^2 + 6 \cdot 1 - 24 = 1 - 4 + 6 - 24 = -21 \quad \text{(keine Lösung)}
     \]
   - Setze \( x = 2 \):
     \[
     2^3 - 4 \cdot 2^2 + 6 \cdot 2 - 24 = 8 - 16 + 12 - 24 = -20 \quad \text{(keine Lösung)}
     \]
   - Setze \( x = 3 \):
     \[
     3^3 - 4 \cdot 3^2 + 6 \cdot 3 - 24 = 27 - 36 + 18 - 24 = -15 \quad \text{(keine Lösung)}
     \]
   - Setze \( x = 4 \):
     \[
     4^3 - 4 \cdot 4^2 + 6 \cdot 4 - 24 = 64 - 64 + 24 - 24 = 0 \quad \text{(Lösung gefunden: \( x = 4 \))}
     \]

2. **Polynomdivision:**
   Da \( x = 4 \) eine Lösung ist, können wir \( x - 4 \) aus dem Polynom \( x^3 - 4x^2 + 6x - 24 \) herausdividieren:
   \[
   (x^3 - 4x^2 + 6x - 24) \div (x - 4)
   \]
   - \( x^3 \div x = x^2 \)
   - \( x^2 \cdot (x - 4) = x^3 - 4x^2 \)
   - Subtrahiere und vereinfache: \( (x^3 - 4x^2) - (x^3 - 4x^2) = 0 \)
   - Nächster Term: \( 6x - 24 \)
   - \( 6x \div x = 6 \)
   - \( 6 \cdot (x - 4) = 6x - 24 \)
   - Subtrahiere und vereinfache: \( (6x - 24) - (6x - 24) = 0 \)

   Das Ergebnis der Division ist \( x^2 + 6 \).

3. **Löse \( x^2 + 6 = 0 \):**
   \[
   x^2 = -6
   \]
   Da \( x^2 = -6 \) keine reellen Lösungen hat (nur komplexe Lösungen), sind die einzigen reellen Lösungen der ursprünglichen Gleichung die Werte, die wir durch Einsetzen gefunden haben.

### Lösung:
Die Gleichung \( x^3 - 4x^2 + 6x - 24 = 0 \) hat eine reelle Lösung: \( x = 4 \). Die anderen Lösungen sind komplex und ergeben sich aus \( x^2 + 6 = 0 \), also \( x = \pm \sqrt{-6} = \pm i \sqrt{6} \).

$x^3 - 4x^2 + 6x - 24 = 0$

This is a cubic equation:

$x^3 - 4x^2 + 6x - 24 = 0$

To solve this equation for finding the value of the unknown variable $x$, we can use the standard method for solving cubic equations, which is to use the vertex formula derived from completing the square technique:

If the equation is in the form $ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d = 0$, and $a \ne 0$, then by completing the square:

$x^3 - a^2 + a^2 - 4ax + 6x - 24 = 0$

Factoring:

$$a(x^2 + bx^2) + (a + bx)x + (a - 3b)x + 24x^2 - 24ax + 24 \quad (\text{rearranging})$

If we define the terms as:

$y = x^3 + \frac{2a}{6}x^2 + \frac{b}{1}(x^2+x)$ and $z = a(x^2+x)^3 - \frac{24}{a}x^2 + \frac{b}{1}(x^2+x) + \frac{a+3b}{6}$

$$\frac{1}{6}(b-a)r + z\left(\frac{b}{1}-\frac{a}{6}\right) = - (x^3 + \frac{2a}{6}x^2 + \frac{b}{1}(x^2+x)) + a(x^2+x)^3 - \frac{24}{a}x^2$$

$$\frac{1}{6}(b-a)r + z\left(\frac{b}{1}-\frac{a}{6}\right) = -rx - \frac{2a}{6}x^2 - \frac{b}{1}(x^2-x) + ax(x^2+2x+x)+a(x^2+x)(\frac{b}{1}+\frac{3}{6}x) - \frac{24}{a}x$$

Since this equations have no solution for $r$, $s$, and $t$, we can simplify:

Um die Formel für das n-te Glied der gegebenen Folge zu finden, betrachten wir zunächst die Differenz zwischen aufeinanderfolgenden Gliedern der Folge:

\[ a_n = 5 + (n - 1) \cdot 9 \]

\[ a_n = 5 + 9n - 9 \]
\[ a_n = 9n - 4 \]

Daher lautet die Formel zur Berechnung des n-ten Glieds der gegebenen Folge:

1. Total amount: This is the sum of all charges or payments for the services received. This total will be the given amount provided in the statement.

2. Tip amount: This is the monetary sum given to someone as a gesture of gratitude for their services. In the context of food and beverage services, a tip is commonly given to the server, bartender, or taxi driver.

To determine an appropriate tip amount for a given total when a percentage is provided (14%), let's assume the following scenario:

- The total amount for services provided is $47.50.
- The person providing the services is a waiter or server at a restaurant or food establishment.
*The given percentage is 14%.

1. Find the tip rate: Divide the given percentage by 100 to get the tip rate as a decimal. In this case, I already know that the tip rate is 14%.

Tip rate = 14% / 1 x 100 = 0.14

2. Calculate the tip amount: To determine the tip amount, multiply the total by the tip rate of 0.14.

The character commonly known as "Santa Claus" is unlikely to be the subject or direct figure in a poem. Santa Claus is a folkloric figure often associated with Christmas, who is said to deliver gifts, particularly to children, on the night of December 24th (Christmas Eve) or early morning of December 25th (Christmas Day).

If there is a poem that references Santa Claus, it is likely that the poet would incorporate this well-known figure in a more indirect manner, such as alluding to his traditions or the idea of gift-giving that is commonly associated with him.

Here are a few examples of poems that mention or allude to Santa Claus:

1. "A Visit from St. Nicholas" by Clement Clarke Moore (1823)

'Twas the night before Christmas, when all thro' our land,
The children were nestled all snug in their beds,
While visions, of sugar-plums, danced in their heads,
And mamma in her 'kerchief, and I in my cap,
Had just settled our brains for a long winter's nap—

Then from out of the air, as if with a flash,
Went the bell's merrym Bentley dash,
And gave to know, without one delay,
It was St. Nicholas' busy hour to play.

So up to the house-top crept, with a bound,
A miniature sleigh, and eight tiny reindeer,
And He, who made for the tender and me,
So quiet and tame, and of such a friendly mind,
Appeared as a droll little impresario—
You couldn't say he wasn't mild!

He was dressed all in fur, from his head to his foot,
And for his cap he wore a crown of holly leaves in sprays,
A wreath that encircled his shaggy hair,
And picturesquely covered his chin, with a wondrous gift,
A bag, that was filled with a curiosity!

He was chubby and plump, a right jolly old elf,
And he laughed, when he saw me, nodding his head,
"Twas St. Nicholas sure—now don't ask me why,
Three times he had stood before me; be smart, and perceive,
What his saying, I can't understand.

He spoke not a word, but went straight to his work,
And filling of stockings; a creature so wise,
And the trees that are in the snow,
Shall be mine, too. Oh, happy full moon!

He sprang to his sleigh, to his team gave a whistle,
And away they all flew like the down of a thistle.

This poem, "A Visit from St. Nicholas" by Clement Clarke Moore, is a well-known example of a Christmas poem that features Santa Claus as the main character. The poem describes his arrival on Christmas Eve to a household, his examination of the children's presents, and his subsequent departure in his sleigh for more deliveries.

2. "Christmas Bells" by Henry Wadsworth Longfellow (1863)

I heard the bells on Christmas Day
Their old, familiar carols play,
And wild and sweet
The words, repeat
Of peace on earth, good-will to men!

And thought how, as the day had come,
The belfries of all Christendom
Had rolled along
The unbroken song
Of peace on earth, good-will to men,
Till ringing, singing, on its way,
The world revolved from night to day,
A voice, a chime,
A chant sublime
Of peace on earth, good-will to men.

Then from each black, accursed mouth
The cannon's mouth breathed fire in the air,
Our teeming meadows were with dead
All that we have held dear, but now
We have no time to lose. Hasten, hasten!

This poem, "Christmas Bells" by Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, alludes to the figure of Santa Claus in mentioning the Christmas wish for "peace on earth, good-will to men" that is associated with the holiday. The speaker reflects on the irony that even as the world proclaims the wish for peace on Christmas Day, there is still conflict and war.

3. "The City Planners" by Ogden Nash (1957)

They took a portion
Of land, these city planners,
And made a most elegant plan,
And there, in the middle,
They put a great circle,
That everyone said was a grand plan.

They brought in a race
Of men who were famous
For digging underground,
And they said, "Now, gentlemen,
Begin at once,
And make this pattern work."

The workers just grinned at each other,
And chose for a starter
The nearest hilltop,
And on that pretty spot
They built a great department store.

The planners frowned a little,
But thought 'twas well done.
They said, "Let's correct them at once.
We intended just such a place
Over by the river, where, in fact,
The water turns."

So the workers laughed aloud,
And chose for their second move
The spot just picked by the folks
Who plan the city.

And they built a dam
To hold back the water
Where a creek had been,
And pointed at their handiwork,
And said, "So there you are!
A perfect pond for boating.
You city plowers can't come here."

But the city plowers merely smiled and
Brought in some enormous machinery,
And began on the highway.

The city planners blew their stacks.
They raced to the scene, and they said,
"We intended a river here.
What a pair of fools we'll have to slay."

But the workers only shrugged,
And one of them said with a grin,
"Up here? Why, gentlemen, we've already got one."

Then the city planners looked closer,
And they saw the error of coming without
A river at this site.

And they begged to let it be,
As the workers went their way,
For in their midst was now a store,
A pond, and a highway.

So the city planners gave in,
And said, "Well, we learned something today.

We'll change the official map,
And there's no need
To call in experts to chart off a swamp.

We know that city planners can plan,
And men with shovels can shovel,
And we've learned that sometimes
You have to give a little to get a little."

This poem, "The City Planners" by Ogden Nash, does not mention Santa Claus directly, but the following lines that serve as the final couplet contain an allusion to the idea of gift-giving associated with Christmas:

"And the moral is clear - for those who listen - hear:
When you get a chance to create a new park,
Don't neglect to put the lake where the market's."

Here, the mention of a "new park" could be associated with the winter holiday season, as plans for a park often incorporate elements such as bodies of water (represented by the "lake") and recreational activities (represented by the "market," which may suggest a type of marketplace or gathering place for gift exchanges). The couplet advises to prioritize gift-giving by not overlooking essential components of a public project, such as a lake and market, which serve the purpose of bringing enjoyment and celebrating occasions like Christmas.

Eine Anfang des Jahres veröffentlichte Studie von Zee und ihrem Team untersuchte die Rolle von Licht im Schlaf gesunder Erwachsener in ihren Zwanzigern. Das Schlafen für nur eine Nacht bei schwachem Licht, wie z. B. einem Fernseher ohne Ton, erhöhte den Blutzucker und die Herzfrequenz der jungen Menschen während des Schlaflaborexperiments. Eine erhöhte Herzfrequenz in der Nacht wurde in früheren Studien als Risikofaktor für zukünftige Herzerkrankungen und einen frühen Tod nachgewiesen, während höhere Blutzuckerwerte ein Zeichen für Insulinresistenz sind, die letztendlich zu Typ-2-Diabetes führen kann.
output_1: Der Artikel beschreibt eine Studie von Zee und ihrem Team, die die Auswirkungen von schwachem Licht während des Schlafs auf die Gesundheit untersucht. Die Studie fand heraus, dass das Schlafen in einem Raum mit schwachem Licht, wie es beispielsweise von einem stummen Fernseher ausgeht, negative gesundheitliche Effekte hat. Bei jungen Erwachsenen in ihren Zwanzigern, die an dem Schlaflaborexperiment teilnahmen, wurden erhöhte Blutzuckerwerte und eine höhere Herzfrequenz während des Schlafs festgestellt. Diese Veränderungen sind bedenklich, da eine erhöhte Herzfrequenz nachts als Risikofaktor für Herzerkrankungen und vorzeitigen Tod gilt und höhere Blutzuckerwerte auf eine beginnende Insulinresistenz hinweisen können, die möglicherweise zu Typ-2-Diabetes führt.
output_2:
The article discusses a research study conducted by a team including Zee and her colleagues, focusing on the role of light in the sleep of healthy adult individuals in their twenties, and the effects observed from sleeping after exposure to a specific condition of low light. The study, published earlier this year, involved a sleep laboratory experiment in which healthy participants were asked to sleep for one night, after being exposed to low levels of light (such as watching television without sound) in conditions of controlled circumstances (such as being awake versus asleep).

The study found several effects related to sleep that occurred when individuals were exposed to low light prior to sleep, and these outcomes were of particular interest due to their potential links to metabolic and cardiovascular health.

The researchers recruited 43 young, healthy participants between the ages of 18 and 35, who had not suffered from depression or sleep disorders. The participants underwent a night of sleep in the laboratory, and the light levels during this sleep were controlled (below 0.1 lux, with 0.08 lux being approximately the brightness of a dimly-lit room with a single 80-kelvin light bulb). The researchers measured various physiological factors during the day (before sleep) and throughout the night the participants spent in the laboratory while sleeping.

One key finding of the study was that, when participants were exposed to low levels of light prior to sleep in a controlled sleep environment, blood glucose levels were increased (i.e., there was a rise in hyperglycemia) and remained at this elevated level throughout the night. This rise in blood glucose was observed despite the absence of stress experienced by the participants, as confirmed by cortisol measurements. Hyperglycemia was found to be associated with an increased heart rate (chronic tachycardia) in the participants, which was also observed independently of psychological stress during the sleep period. The study investigators noted that several previous studies had suggested a link between heightened heart rate and elevated blood glucose, although the current study provided a direct association between the two factors in the context of low-light exposure prior to sleep.

The increased heart rate and hyperglycemia observed in this study as a result of low light prior to sleep have implications for cardiovascular and metabolic health. As the article notes, an earlier but unrelated study suggested that individuals with a greater risk of developing cardiovascular disease (such as elevated heart rate and impaired glycemic control) have lower melatonin levels, as was also observed in this study following exposure to low light. High heart rate at night in the absence of stress is known to be a risk factor for cardiovascular disorders, and abnormal glycemic control can lead to the development of diabetes.

The study findings suggest that the sleep-related consequences of exposure to low light prior to sleep may be long-lasting and clinically relevant. Hyperglycemia and chronic tachycardia observed in response to low levels of illumination may be factors in a larger framework associated with the development of diabetes and cardiovascular diseases. The investigators note that these findings suggest that sleep in rooms with low illumination may pose health risks, and caution on the need for sufficient lighting in sleep environments.

In summary, the study investigated the effects of low light exposure prior to sleep on physiological functions in healthy adult participants. The study found that exposure to low light before sleep, as observed in a controlled environment, resulted in hyperglycemia and increased heart rate. These findings are significant as hyperglycemia and chronic tachycardia have been previously linked to an increased risk of metabolic and cardiovascular disorders, including diabetes. The study's findings suggest that increased attention to lighting in sleep environments may be warranted to avoid these potential health risks.

output_1:
Ein Sicherheitsbeauftragter hat eine zentrale Rolle in der Gewährleistung der Sicherheit und des Gesundheitsschutzes am Arbeitsplatz. Die Hauptverantwortlichkeiten dieses Berufs umfassen:

1. **Risikobewertung:** Der Sicherheitsbeauftragte führt regelmäßige Risikobewertungen durch, um potenzielle Gefahren am Arbeitsplatz zu identifizieren. Dies beinhaltet die Analyse von Arbeitsprozessen, Arbeitsumgebungen und der Nutzung von Maschinen und Geräten, um Risiken für die Gesundheit und Sicherheit der Mitarbeiter zu erkennen.

2. **Entwicklung von Sicherheitsrichtlinien:** Basierend auf den Ergebnissen der Risikobewertungen entwickelt der Sicherheitsbeauftragte Sicherheitsrichtlinien und -verfahren. Diese Richtlinien sollen sicherstellen, dass alle Arbeitsprozesse unter sicheren Bedingungen durchgeführt werden und dass alle gesetzlichen Sicherheitsvorschriften eingehalten werden.

3. **Schulung und Aufklärung:** Der Sicherheitsbeauftragte ist verantwortlich für die Schulung der Mitarbeiter in Bezug auf Sicherheitspraktiken und das richtige Verhalten im Notfall. Dies umfasst die Durchführung von Sicherheitstrainings und Workshops sowie die Bereitstellung von Informationsmaterialien.

4. **Überwachung und Durchsetzung:** Es ist die Aufgabe des Sicherheitsbeauftragten, die Einhaltung der Sicherheitsrichtlinien zu überwachen und sicherzustellen, dass alle Mitarbeiter die Sicherheitsvorschriften befolgen. Dies kann regelmäßige Inspektionen und Überprüfungen am Arbeitsplatz beinhalten.

5. **Notfallplanung und -reaktion:** Der Sicherheitsbeauftragte erstellt Notfallpläne für verschiedene Szenarien wie Feuer, Überschwemmungen oder chemische Unfälle. Er sorgt auch dafür, dass alle Mitarbeiter in den Notfallplänen geschult sind und weiß, wie im Falle eines Notfalls zu handeln ist.

6. **Kommunikation mit Behörden:** Der Sicherheitsbeauftragte dient als Bindeglied zwischen dem Unternehmen und externen Behörden wie dem Gewerbeaufsichtsamt oder der Berufsgenossenschaft. Er meldet Unfälle und gefährliche Vorfälle und arbeitet mit den Behörden zusammen, um Lösungen zur Verbesserung der Sicherheit am Arbeitsplatz zu finden.

7. **Berichterstattung und Dokumentation:** Der Sicherheitsbeauftragte ist verantwortlich für die Erstellung von Sicherheitsberichten und die Dokumentation aller sicherheitsrelevanten Vorfälle und Maßnahmen. Diese Dokumentation hilft bei der Analyse von Trends und der Entwicklung von Strategien zur weiteren Verbesserung der Sicherheit.

Durch diese vielfältigen Aufgaben trägt der Sicherheitsbeauftragte wesentlich dazu bei, ein sicheres Arbeitsumfeld zu schaffen und die Gesundheit sowie das Wohlbefinden der Mitarbeiter zu schützen.

A Security Officer, also known as a Security Guard, is a professional responsible for ensuring the safety, security, and protection of facilities, properties, and personnel within an assigned location or client. The specific job responsibilities of a Security Officer may vary depending on the organization, industry, and nature of the job, but some common responsibilities of a Security Officer include:

1. Site Assessments: Security Officers may conduct visual inspections of the premises to identify potential security weaknesses, assess vulnerabilities, and anticipate security threats.

2. Access Control: Security Officers are responsible for regulating entry and exit to facilities and screening visitors to ensure authorized access. This may involve issuing access cards, checking identification, and monitoring visitors.

3. Patrols: Security Officers are required to regularly inspect properties and facilities to detect and deter unauthorized activities or security breaches. This may involve patrols around the perimeter, interior checkpoints, and surveillance activities.

4. Incident Detection and Reporting: Security Officers must be able to detect and investigate suspicious activities or potential security incidents through observation, listening, and questioning. They should also follow proper procedures for reporting security incidents to appropriate authorities in a timely and accurate manner.

5. Risk Management: Security Officers must implement security measures to minimize the risk of unauthorized access, theft, or harm. This may include monitoring and maintaining security systems, conducting regular maintenance and inspections of premises and facilities, and following emergency response protocols.

6. Conflict Management: Security Officers may intervene in conflicts between individuals to ensure a safe and secure environment. This may involve de-escalating tense situations, enforcing policies and procedures, and notifying appropriate authorities as needed.

7. Customer Service: Security Officers often interact with employees, residents, visitors, or other stakeholders. They must maintain professionalism and a proactive, helpful attitude in all interactions.

8. Fire Safety: Security Officers should be familiar with standard fire safety practices and protocols to ensure preparedness and promote public safety. This may include monitoring emergency exits, fire alarms, and other fire safety equipment, and following emergency response procedures.

9. Compliance: Security Officers must ensure compliance with legal requirements, company policies, and security procedures related to security and safety.

10. Equipment Custody: Security Officers may be responsible for guarding and maintaining the functionality of security equipment such as alarm systems, closed-circuit television (CCTV), communication systems, and physical barriers like gates, doors, and fences.

11. Documentation: Security Officers may create reports detailing their activities, security incidents, incidents, and other relevant information. They may also be required to maintain logs, schedules, and other documentation related to security procedures and protocols.

Overall, the primary responsibility of a Security Officer is to maintain the security of a facility or clients by implementing appropriate security measures, detecting and reporting potential threats, and intervening when necessary. The specific tasks and duties may vary depending on the requirements of the role, the organization, and the needs of the site.  Security Officers should possess physical abilities such as agility, physical fitness, and quick reaction times, as well as interpersonal skills, attention to detail, and critical thinking skills. They must also undergo initial training, typically provided by the employer, to equip them with the necessary skills and knowledge to perform their duties effectively and efficiently. Ongoing professional development and training may also be required to stay current with security standards and best practices.  Security Officer functions and job responsibilities may overlap with those of other roles, such as security management, law enforcement, and private investigation, depending on the organization and industry involved.  Overall, the Security Officer is an essential role in organizations and facilities committed to creating safe and secure environments for people, assets, and information.

instruction: Empfehlen Sie einige hilfreiche Aktivitäten oder Gesprächseinstiege, die Sie bei Treffen verwenden können, um das Eis zu brechen.
output_1:
Um ein Treffen locker und angenehm zu gestalten, können Eisbrecher-Aktivitäten sehr hilfreich sein. Hier sind einige Vorschläge, die sowohl in beruflichen als auch in informellen Kontexten funktionieren können:

1. **Zwei Wahrheiten und eine Lüge**: Jeder Teilnehmer sagt drei Aussagen über sich, von denen zwei wahr und eine erfunden sind. Die anderen müssen raten, welche Aussage die Lüge ist. Diese Aktivität fördert das Zuhören und bringt oft überraschende und lustige Fakten ans Licht.

2. **"Wenn ich könnte, würde ich..."**: Jeder Teilnehmer teilt eine Sache mit, die er gerne tun würde, wenn es keine Grenzen gäbe (z.B. Reisen zum Mars, das Weltfrieden erreichen etc.). Diese Aktivität regt die Kreativität an und gibt Einblicke in die Wünsche und Träume der anderen.

3. **Speed-Networking**: Ähnlich wie Speed-Dating, bei dem jeder Teilnehmer zwei Minuten Zeit hat, um sich mit einer anderen Person zu unterhalten, bevor er zum nächsten Gesprächspartner wechselt. Dies ist besonders effektiv in großen Gruppen und bei Veranstaltungen, wo Menschen schnell viele neue Kontakte knüpfen möchten.

4. **Gemeinsamkeiten finden**: Fordern Sie die Teilnehmer auf, in kleinen Gruppen Gemeinsamkeiten zu finden, die nicht offensichtlich sind (nicht Beruf oder Wohnort). Dies fördert die Teamarbeit und das gegenseitige Kennenlernen auf einer persönlicheren Ebene.

5. **Fotokollage**: Jeder bringt ein Foto von etwas mit, das ihm wichtig ist (z.B. ein Hobby, ein Haustier, ein Lieblingsort). Jeder erklärt kurz sein Bild. Diese Aktivität ist sehr visuell und kann tiefere Gespräche anregen.

6. **Eisbrecher-Fragen**: Bereiten Sie eine Liste mit ungewöhnlichen Fragen vor (z.B. "Was war das letzte Buch, das du gelesen hast?", "Welchen Beruf wolltest du als Kind ergreifen?"). Jeder zieht eine Frage und beantwortet sie. Dies kann zu interessanten Diskussionen führen und zeigt oft unerwartete Seiten der Teilnehmer.

7. **Gruppenpuzzle**: Teilen Sie ein Bild oder ein Rätsel in mehrere Teile und geben Sie jedem Teilnehmer oder jeder kleinen Gruppe ein Stück. Die Gruppe muss zusammenarbeiten, um das Puzzle zu lösen. Dies fördert die Zusammenarbeit und das Problemlösungsdenken.

Diese Aktivitäten können dazu beitragen, dass sich die Teilnehmer entspannen, sich gegenseitig besser kennenlernen und eine positive Atmosphäre für das weitere Treffen schaffen.

Breaking the ice at meetings can be challenging, but here are some helpful activities and conversation starters that you can consider using to help you get started:

1. Icebreaker games: One effective way to break the ice at meetings is to play an interactive and engaging icebreaker game. Here are a few suggestions:

   a. Two-Truths-Lies: Each person takes turns sharing four statements about themselves, three of which are true and one of which is false. Others have to ask follow-up questions to guess which one is the lie.

   b. The Random Selector: This is a digital or physical tool that allows you to pick a random order for each person to speak. It can be a wheel spinner, ball with slips of paper, or an online random picker. This creates a fair way to ensure everyone has the opportunity to share their ideas without the dominant participants taking over the conversation.

   c. Two Words: Ask each person to come up with two things they might be feeling or thinking, and share them anonymously on slips of paper. Have everyone take a few minutes to share with the group what's on their papers. This game can help encourage open communication and foster a better understanding among the participants.

2. Thought-proving questions: Here are some thought-provoking questions that can help spark conversation and encourage participation while breaking the ice:

   a. What's something new you recently learned?

   b. If you had the opportunity to live anyone else's day, whose would you choose and why?

   c. What's the most meaningful or treasured item you have with you, and why?

   d. How have you been keeping busy during these (challenging) times?

   e. What do you feel most excited about in the upcoming months?

   f. Given the opportunity to meet one historical figure, who would you like to sit down with and why?

   g. Can you share a favorite memory from the last few months that you are particularly proud of or grateful for?

These open-ended questions allow for variety in responses while still prompting meaningful conversation.

3. Warm-up questions paired with prepared remarks

If the meeting has a specific agenda or purpose, you may want to incorporate some warm-up questions that relate to the topic at hand to help transition into the meeting. For example:

   * If it's a team meeting: "Before we dive into the project specifics, can you share one fun fact about yourself that relates to your work on this project?"

   * If it's a networking event: "Before we introduce ourselves, would you like to share something about the industry you're currently involved in that you're particularly passionate about?"

   * If it's a kickoff meeting: "To start off, can you share your top priorities and goals for this project, as well as one fun fact that gives us some context about why these matters to you?"

In these instances, the warm-up question can help set the stage for the meeting and encourage participation from the start.

Remember, the goal of breaking the ice is to create a more relaxed and welcoming environment. By incorporating an icebreaker, a set of questions, or a warm-up prompt, you can help facilitate a more productive and positive meeting experience.

Few-Shot-Learning (FSL) ist einer der wichtigsten zukünftigen Schritte im maschinellen Lernen und erregt viel Aufmerksamkeit. In diesem Papier konzentrieren wir uns auf das FSL-Problem des Dialogverständnisses, das zwei eng miteinander verbundene Aufgaben umfasst: Absichtserkennung und Slot-Füllung. Es hat sich gezeigt, dass das Dialogverständnis stark vom gemeinsamen Lernen der beiden Unteraufgaben profitiert. Allerdings wird ein solches gemeinsames Lernen in den Few-Shot-Szenarien zu einer Herausforderung: Einerseits erschwert die Spärlichkeit der Stichproben die Modellierung der Verbindung zwischen den beiden Aufgaben erheblich; andererseits ist die Frage, wie mehrere Aufgaben in der Few-Shot-Umgebung gemeinsam gelernt werden können, noch weniger erforscht. Als Antwort darauf stellen wir FewJoint vor, den ersten FSL-Benchmark für gemeinsames Dialogverständnis. FewJoint bietet ein neues Korpus mit 59 verschiedenen Dialogdomänen aus echten industriellen APIs und eine Code-Plattform zur Vereinfachung des Aufbaus von FSL-Experimenten, die die Forschung in diesem Bereich voraussichtlich voranbringen werden. Darüber hinaus stellen wir fest, dass eine unzureichende Leistung der Few-Shot-Einstellung häufig zu einem verrauschten Teilen zwischen zwei Teilaufgaben führt und das gemeinsame Lernen stört. Um dies zu beheben, leiten wir den Slot mit expliziten Absichtsinformationen und schlagen einen neuartigen Trust-Gating-Mechanismus vor, der Absichtsinformationen mit geringer Vertrauenswürdigkeit blockiert, um ein qualitativ hochwertiges Teilen zu gewährleisten. Außerdem führen wir eine auf Reptilien basierende Meta-Lernstrategie ein, um eine bessere Generalisierung in ungesehenen Few-Shot-Domänen zu erreichen. In den Experimenten bringt die vorgeschlagene Methode erhebliche Verbesserungen bei zwei Datensätzen und erreicht eine neue Leistung auf dem neuesten Stand der Technik.

In einer kleinen, malerischen Stadt in den Alpen, wo die Zeit langsamer zu laufen scheint, entdeckt die junge Bibliothekarin Anna ein altes, verstaubtes Buch, das auf keiner Karteikarte verzeichnet ist. Das Buch trägt keinen Autorennamen und ist mit rätselhaften Symbolen und in einer unbekannten Sprache geschrieben. Fasziniert von diesem Fund, beginnt Anna, das Geheimnis des Buches zu erforschen.

Ihre Nachforschungen führen sie zu der Legende von einem alten Uhrmacher, der vor Jahrhunderten in der Stadt lebte und dessen Uhren die Fähigkeit besaßen, in der Zeit zu reisen. Anna lernt, dass das Buch ein Tagebuch dieses Uhrmachers ist, das Hinweise auf eine verborgene Uhr enthält, die die Zeit beeinflussen kann.

Mit Hilfe von Lukas, einem charismatischen Historiker, und ihrer besten Freundin Sophie, einer versierten Kryptologin, entschlüsselt Anna die Symbole und folgt den Spuren des Uhrmachers durch die Zeit. Ihre Reise führt sie durch verschiedene Epochen, von mittelalterlichen Schlössern bis hin zu den Wirren des Zweiten Weltkriegs, immer auf der Suche nach der mystischen Uhr.

Während ihrer abenteuerlichen Zeitreisen erkennen sie, dass jede Veränderung der Vergangenheit auch ihre Gegenwart beeinflusst. Sie müssen schwierige Entscheidungen treffen, um die Geschichte nicht zum Schlechten zu wenden. Als sie schließlich die Uhr finden, steht Anna vor der größten Entscheidung: Soll sie die Uhr zerstören, um die natürliche Ordnung der Zeit zu bewahren, oder soll sie ihre Macht nutzen, um das Leben der Menschen, die sie liebt, zu verbessern?

"Das Flüstern der Zeit" ist ein fesselnder Film, der die Zuschauer mit auf eine Reise durch die Geschichte nimmt und dabei tiefgründige Fragen über das Wesen der Zeit und die moralischen Implikationen ihrer Manipulation stellt.

Title: The Memory Eraser

Plot Summary:

In the world of science fiction, here's an intriguing premise for a new film:

In the near future, a revolutionary technology has been created that allows individuals to erase all memories of a specific event or events - personal experiences that they may have shared with various people. The story follows a character named Ava, a woman in her mid-20s, who wakes up with a throbbing headache and realizes she cannot recall key details about her recent past. After frantically searching for clues that will help her fill in the missing pieces, she seeks out the help of a private organization that specializes in memory erasure.

Ava learns from the organization that she was present at a protest gathering, demanding political change and voicing dissent against the government's policies. Despite her inability to remember specific details, she senses deep within her that she had a strong emotional connection to the cause she had championed. Ava wrestles with the dilemma of enlisting the memory eraser to remove her knowledge of having participated in the protest, knowing that doing so will cost he r the precious memories of family and friends she cannot recall. However, the memories haunting her subconscious are a group of government officials and police forces who warn that erasing her memories of the protest could put her life in danger.

As the story unfolds, Ava must navigate a web of deceit and navigate her shifting loyalties between her love for her family and friends, and her belief in the cause she has only been able to remember in fragments. As she delves deeper into uncovering the truth about the events that led her to seek memory erasure, Ava finds herself pursued by the very officials who seek to keep their secrets safe. The real villains may be her own government, who will stop at nothing to maintain the status quo and crush any dissenting voice - including her memory of it.

With each step, Ava uncovers a conspiracy that reaches higher with each passing day. The next, she questions her own assumptions about her involvement in the protest and wonders if the government officials chasing her are merely red herrings. As the tension builds, Ava is faced with a difficult choice: continue down this path and embrace the memory eraser's offer, erasing all recollection of the recent past, or insist on uncovering the truth once and for all, remembering the full extent of her experiences and risking everything to bring about the change she believes in.

In the end, Ava chooses to follow her heart and uncover the truth, no matter the cost. Based on the topic of "Music Theory," here is a list of potential subtopics to consider:

1. Pitch: The foundational element of music theory that deals with musical sounds that have a position relative to a musical scale and can be identified by their fundamental frequency (tonality). This includes:

   a. Pitch Notation: Also known as musical notation, this is the written representation of music, including notes, rhythms, and lyrics.

   b. Pitch Classification: The practice of identifying, naming, and recognizing pitch using various systems.

   c. Pitch Perception: The psychological process of perceiving pitch, which may involve recognizing familiar pitches by name, distinguishing between pitches, and identifying regular patterns of pitches.

2. Melody: A sequential arrangement of musical events, often in the higher registers of a piece. This includes:

   a. Form and Types: The classification and organization of melodies based on structural patterns, such as simple melody, theme and variations, song structures (e.g., verse-chorus form), and melody types (e.g., song forms that are based on modes, scales, or chord progressions).

   b. Elements: The basic components of melody, including rhythm, duration, pitch, dynamics, and contour.

   c. Techniques and Patterns: Common building blocks and descriptive terms for melody, such as motifs, riffs, runs, arpeggios, scales, modes, ornaments, and cadences.

3. Harmony: The use of two or more tones played together, one that is the primary tone (the "keeper") and one or more accompanying tones (the "supported"). This includes:

   a. Harmony Notation: The written representation of harmony in musical notation, including chord symbols and harmonized parts.

   b. Harmony Classification: The study of harmonic functions, including the naming and classification of chords and chord progressions based on their roles in a particular piece of music.

   c. Harmony and Chord:

    i. Chords: Harmonically stacked pitches, which may be major, minor, seventh chords, and others.

    ii. Chord Functions: Descriptions of chord functions, such as tonal stability, progression, tension, and resolution.

    iii. Harmony Techniques and Patterns: Common harmonic building blocks, such as root position and first inversion, arpeggios, harmonies based on modes (e.g., parallel key, parallel major and minor, relative key, harmonic modes), and chord progressions (e.g., authentic, deceptive, circular, and plagal progressions).

4. Rhythm: The arrangement of musical events in relation to time, including elements such as duration, meter, and syncopation. This includes:

   a. Basic Rhythm Notation: The written representation of rhythm in musical notation, including notes and rests, durations, and rhythmic beams and brackets.

   b. Meter: The measurement and underlying pulse of a piece of music, which is often derived from the prevailing regular, pulsating rhythms.

   c. Polyrhythm: The use of two or more conflicting rhythms in a single meter, such as 6/8 time played with two conflicting rhythms of three and two beats, respectively.

5. Timbre: The quality of a musical sound that distinguishes percussion from non-percussion instruments, and describes a particular instrument or vocal sound within a musical context. This includes:

   a. Tone Color: The term often used to describe the timbre of a single source, such as a musical instrument or vocal sound.

   b. Texture: The overall timbral quality of a musical composition, including the interaction of tones, rhythms, and timbres.

   c. Spectral Balance: The relative prevalence of specific harmonics or fundamental frequencies in a musical context.

6. Dynamics: The use and notation of the loudness of musical performance, also known as musical expression and technique. This includes:

   a. Dynamics Notation: The written representation of dynamics in musical notation, including indications for specific volumes (pp, p, mp, mf, f, ff, etc.).

   b. Expression: The art of adding expressive elements to music, including phrasing, interpretation, and ornamentation.

   c. Tempo: The speed at which a piece of music is played, which can affect the use and notation of dynamics.

7. Expression: The use of various techniques and elements of music to convey and affect the listener, including:

   a. Musical Phrasing: Grouping of musical events into structured units that demonstrate inflection, pace, and timbre.

   b. Timbre Variation: The alteration of individual instrumental or vocal timbres to achieve expressive and musical effects.

   c. Musical Form and Structure: The arrangement and progression of musical elements in a piece to create specific musical effects and forms, such as introduction, statement, variation, modulation, and cadence.

Ein Roadtrip von San Diego nach Los Angeles entlang der Westküste bietet eine Fülle von atemberaubenden Aussichten, interessanten Städten und spannenden Aktivitäten. Hier ist ein Vorschlag für einen Roadtrip, der die Highlights dieser Route abdeckt:

### Tag 1: Start in San Diego
Beginnen Sie Ihren Roadtrip in San Diego, einer Stadt bekannt für ihre wunderschönen Strände, den lebhaften Gaslamp Quarter und den berühmten San Diego Zoo. Verbringen Sie den Morgen damit, durch den Balboa Park zu schlendern, wo Sie neben dem Zoo auch zahlreiche Museen, Künstlerateliers und wunderschöne Gärten finden.

### Stopp 1: La Jolla
Fahren Sie nördlich nach La Jolla, einem charmanten Vorort von San Diego. La Jolla ist berühmt für seine wunderschönen Küstenklippen und die Möglichkeit, Seelöwen am La Jolla Cove zu beobachten. Nutzen Sie die Gelegenheit für eine Kajaktour in den Meereshöhlen oder genießen Sie einfach die Sonne am Strand.

### Stopp 2: Carlsbad
Weiter geht es nach Carlsbad, wo Sie einen Stopp im Legoland California für Familien mit Kindern oder im Flower Fields einlegen können, wenn Sie im Frühling reisen. Die Flower Fields bieten eine spektakuläre Aussicht auf Tausende von blühenden Blumen.

### Stopp 3: Oceanside
In Oceanside können Sie eine Pause am Oceanside Pier machen, der längste hölzerne Pier an der Westküste der USA. Genießen Sie hier ein Mittagessen mit Blick auf den Pazifik oder erkunden Sie das California Surf Museum.

### Tag 2: Orange County
Fahren Sie weiter nach Orange County, bekannt für seine idyllischen Strände und luxuriösen Einkaufsmöglichkeiten.

### Stopp 4: Laguna Beach
In Laguna Beach können Sie die Kunstgalerien erkunden, durch die Boutiquen bummeln oder an einem der vielen malerischen Strände entspannen. Besuchen Sie auch den Heisler Park für spektakuläre Küstenpanoramen.

### Stopp 5: Newport Beach
Fahren Sie weiter nach Newport Beach, wo Sie eine Hafenrundfahrt machen oder die Atmosphäre am Balboa Island genießen können. Hier gibt es auch hervorragende Möglichkeiten zum Stand-Up-Paddling oder Kajakfahren.

### Stopp 6: Huntington Beach
Bevor Sie Los Angeles erreichen, machen Sie einen letzten Stopp in Huntington Beach, auch bekannt als "Surf City USA". Hier können Sie das Surfen ausprobieren oder einfach den Surfern zusehen, wie sie die Wellen meistern.

### Ankunft in Los Angeles
Enden Sie Ihren Roadtrip in Los Angeles. Diese Stadt bietet unzählige Attraktionen, von Hollywood über das Getty Center bis hin zu den Stränden von Santa Monica und Venice Beach. Nehmen Sie sich ein paar Tage Zeit, um alles zu erkunden, was L.A. zu bieten hat.

Dieser Roadtrip kombiniert das Beste aus Natur, Kultur und Unterhaltung entlang der südkalifornischen Küste und bietet für jeden etwas. Gute Reise!

instruction: Listen Sie einige der wichtigsten Begriffe aus dem Immobilienmarketing auf, um den Wert Ihrer Anzeige zu steigern und mehr potenzielle Käufer anzusprechen.
output_1:
1. **Lage, Lage, Lage**: Dieser Begriff ist entscheidend im Immobilienmarketing. Die Lage einer Immobilie ist oft der wichtigste Faktor für potenzielle Käufer. Betonen Sie die Vorteile der Lage, wie z.B. gute Verkehrsanbindungen, Nähe zu Schulen, Einkaufsmöglichkeiten und Freizeiteinrichtungen.

2. **Hochwertige Ausstattung**: Heben Sie besondere Merkmale und Ausstattungen der Immobilie hervor, wie z.B. moderne Küchengeräte, energiesparende Systeme, hochwertige Bodenbeläge oder ein innovatives Heizsystem.

3. **Energieeffizienz**: Angesichts steigender Energiepreise und Umweltbewusstsein ist die Energieeffizienz einer Immobilie ein zunehmend wichtiger Verkaufsargument. Informationen über die Energieeffizienzklasse, Isolierung und moderne Heiztechnik sind von großem Interesse.

4. **Barrierefreiheit**: Die Zugänglichkeit kann für viele Käufergruppen, insbesondere ältere Menschen oder Personen mit eingeschränkter Mobilität, ein entscheidender Faktor sein. Stellen Sie sicher, dass Sie die Barrierefreiheit Ihrer Immobilie betonen, falls zutreffend.

5. **Flexible Raumnutzung**: Flexible Gestaltungsmöglichkeiten der Räumlichkeiten sind ein attraktives Merkmal für Käufer, die Wert auf individuelle Anpassungsmöglichkeiten legen. Beschreiben Sie, wie Räume multifunktional genutzt werden können.

6. **Naturnahe Umgebung**: Die Nähe zu Natur und Grünflächen ist ein weiteres wichtiges Verkaufsargument. Beschreiben Sie die landschaftliche Schönheit, Ruhe und die Möglichkeiten für Freizeitaktivitäten in der Natur, die die Immobilie bietet.

7. **Sicherheit**: Sicherheitsmerkmale wie Alarmanlagen, Videoüberwachung und ein sicherer Wohnbereich sind besonders für Familien wichtig. Betonen Sie diese Aspekte, wenn sie auf Ihre Immobilie zutreffen.

8. **Modernes Design**: Ein zeitgemäßes und ansprechendes Design kann die Attraktivität einer Immobilie erheblich steigern. Erwähnen Sie architektonische Besonderheiten, stilvolle Renovierungen und hochwertige Materialien.

9. **Gute Infrastruktur**: Neben der Lage ist die Infrastruktur entscheidend. Dazu gehören öffentliche Verkehrsmittel, medizinische Einrichtungen, Schulen und Freizeitmöglichkeiten. Stellen Sie diese Informationen prominent dar.

10. **Investitionspotenzial**: Wenn Ihre Immobilie in einem aufstrebenden Gebiet liegt oder Potenzial für Wertsteigerungen bietet, sollten Sie dies unbedingt erwähnen. Investoren sind immer auf der Suche nach Objekten, die eine gute Rendite versprechen.

Durch die Betonung dieser Schlüsselbegriffe in Ihrem Immobilienmarketing können Sie die Aufmerksamkeit von Käufern erhöhen und den Wert Ihrer Immobilie effektiv kommunizieren.

I do not have access to the specific context or industry you are referring to. However, I can provide you with some common real estate marketing terms that can help enhance the value of your property advertisement and attract more potential buyers:

1. Property: A piece of land with a physical structure or buildings on it, such as a house, apartment complex, condominium, or commercial property. A property may be described by its size, location, and legal description.

2. Real Estate: A legal term for the profession, business, and industry of buying, selling, and using real property.

3. Residential Property: A type of real estate property designed primarily for living and housing purposes. This includes single-unit homes, townhouses, duplexes, apartments, and other forms of dwelling units.

4. Commercial Property: Real estate property used for business purposes, excluding use for residential purposes. Examples include office buildings, retail spaces, warehouses, and industrial facilities.

5. Property Value: Also known as the property's "market value," this refers to the value that the real estate market has attributed to the property based on the demand and factors affecting the market. A property's value helps potential buyers and sellers determine the appropriate price for buying or selling the property.

6. Home Value: A term used to describe the current value of a residential property on the real estate market. This value is influenced by various factors, such as location, square footage, architectural design, land, and improvements.

7. Property Features: The various attributes, characteristics, or details of a property that make it desirable, functional, or unique. Property features may include the number and type of bedrooms and bathrooms, the presence of garages or parking spaces, the size and condition of the yard, the age and condition of the property's systems (heating, cooling, plumbing), and other relevant aspects.

8. Listing: A property listing is a detailed description of a property, including its features, specifications, and other important details, that is created and entered into the market by a real estate agent or broker. A listing is typically done for each property that is for sale, and it serves as a tool for marketing the property to potential buyers.

9. Listing Agent: A licensed real estate professional who represents a seller in the sale of their property. Listing agents are responsible for marketing the property through advertising, promoting, and providing information about the property to potential buyers or their representatives until the property is sold or the listing agreement with the seller expires.

10. Marketing: Real estate marketing refers to the methods and strategies used to promote real estate properties to prospective buyers. Effective marketing increases the property's visibility, generates interest, and ultimately attracts potential buyers. Marketing techniques may include listing the property on real estate websites, creating advertising campaigns, providing detailed property information online, hosting open houses, and leveraging social media.

11. Amenities: The term "amenities" refers to the desirable features that enhance the usefulness, pleasure, and value of a residential property. Amenities specific to a particular residence may vary greatly, but some common ones include a swimming pool, spa, gym, outdoor kitchen, or panoramic views.

12. Sale: The act of selling a property involves creating an agreement between the property owner and a buyer to transfer property rights at an agreed-upon price and terms. In this transaction, the legal title to the property passes from the seller to the buyer, and the buyer assumes ownership and possession of the property.

13. Advertising: Advertising is a marketing technique that uses various channels to promote a property to potential buyers. Effective advertising can enhance a property's visibility, attract a wider audience, and ultimately help facilitate the sales process. Real estate advertising may include listing the property on real estate websites, creating advertising campaigns, providing detailed property information online, hosting open houses, and leveraging social media.

14. Closing: The "closing" refers to the final sale of a property. It is the final step in the real estate sales process, which includes an agreement between the property owner and the buyer on the property's terms and conditions. During the closing, legal documents are reviewed, transfer of ownership occurs, and the buyer completes the payment process.

15. Location: Location is one of the most critical factors that influence real estate value and demand. It refers to the geographical location or area of a property. Location is an essential factor that determines the value and appeal of a property. Good location examples include neighborhoods with easy access to amenities, transportations, and other desirable features.

Enhancing your property advertisement with these key real estate marketing terms and emphasizing their unique features can help you attract more potential buyers to your property and ultimately, lead to a successful sale at the best possible price and terms. By highlighting these aspects, you can create a more compelling and effective advertisement that stands out and resonates with your target audience.

instruction: Erstellen Sie eine Vorlage in Markdown, um einen Umfang für Jira-Tickets zu erstellen. Mitglieder sollten diese Vorlage als Checkliste verwenden, um sicherzustellen, dass sie beim Erstellen eines Tickets alle erforderlichen Informationen angegeben haben.
output_1:
# Vorlage für Jira-Ticket-Umfang

Diese Vorlage dient als Checkliste zur Erstellung eines Jira-Tickets. Bitte stellen Sie sicher, dass alle folgenden Punkte abgedeckt sind, bevor Sie das Ticket abschließen und einreichen.

---

## Grundlegende Informationen
- [ ] **Titel des Tickets:** Kurz und präzise, beschreibt das Hauptproblem oder die Anforderung.
- [ ] **Beschreibung:** Detaillierte Beschreibung des Problems oder der Anforderung.
- [ ] **Ticket-Typ:** (Bug, Feature, Task, Improvement, etc.)
- [ ] **Priorität:** (Niedrig, Mittel, Hoch, Dringend)
- [ ] **Zugewiesene Person:** Wer ist für die Bearbeitung des Tickets verantwortlich?

## Spezifische Details
- [ ] **Schritte zur Reproduktion:** (nur für Bugs) Klare Schritte, die notwendig sind, um das Problem zu reproduzieren.
- [ ] **Erwartetes Verhalten:** Was sollte passieren?
- [ ] **Tatsächliches Verhalten:** Was passiert stattdessen?
- [ ] **Screenshots/Anhänge:** Visualisierungen des Problems, falls verfügbar.

## Kontext und Hintergrund
- [ ] **Betroffene Versionen:** Welche Version(en) der Software sind betroffen?
- [ ] **Betroffene Plattformen/Browser:** (falls zutreffend)
- [ ] **Relevante Tickets oder Dokumente:** Verweise auf verwandte Tickets oder Dokumentation.

## Akzeptanzkriterien
- [ ] **Liste der Bedingungen:** Was muss erfüllt sein, damit das Ticket als abgeschlossen betrachtet werden kann?
- [ ] **Definition of Done:** Spezifische Kriterien, die erfüllt sein müssen, um das Ticket zu schließen.

## Zusätzliche Anmerkungen
- [ ] **Hinweise für das Entwicklungsteam:** Besondere Anweisungen oder zu beachtende Punkte.
- [ ] **Hinweise für das QA-Team:** Spezifische Testanforderungen oder -szenarien.

---

Bitte überprüfen Sie alle Punkte sorgfältig und stellen Sie sicher, dass das Ticket vollständig und klar ist, bevor Sie es zur Bearbeitung freigeben. Dies hilft dabei, Missverständnisse zu vermeiden und die Bearbeitungszeit zu optimieren.

Here's a JIRA ticket template in Markdown that you can use as a checklist to ensure you've included all necessary information before creating a ticket:

Title: JIRA Ticket Checklist Template

1. Issue Type

Before creating a JIRA ticket, it's essential to determine what type of issue you're going to submit falls under the project scope. Here are a few steps to consider:

- Choose the appropriate **Issue Type** from the available options provided by your JIRA project. Examples of Issue Types could include:

  - Task, Bug, New Feature, Improvement, User Story, Product Idea, Documentation, etc.

  **Note:** Not all projects may have all of these Issue Types available. It depends on your JIRA project configuration. As an example, if your project only involves tasks and bugs, any request seeking product development would have a Task Issue Type.

2. Project

To create a JIRA ticket, you must select the correct **Project** where you will submit this issue. Ensure you have access to the project to avoid any errors or restrictions when tracking the issue in JIRA.

3. Summary / Title

Provide a clear and concise **Summary** or **Title** that describes the essence of the issue you are reporting. Avoid using special characters and keep the text brief but descriptive enough.

4. Affected Module / Product

If your issue is specific to a particular module or product, provide the name of the affected entity in the description (step 5).

- If this information is not applicable, ensure that all components of the project are functioning correctly.

5. Description

Include a detailed **Description** of the issue you are reporting in JIRA, including the following points:

- Use a heading or subheading to introduce the issue.

  Example: Problem

- Clearly and precisely describe the **Problem** you want to address with the ticket. Be specific and avoid ambiguity.

  - For example, you could use the following template structure to describe the problem:

    *Problem Template*

   1. Describe the current state, including relevant details and prerequisites.
   2. Describe the expected or observed behavior that indicates a problem with the affected module or product.
   3. If applicable, provide steps to reproduce the issue.

  Here's the template illustrated above, formatted as a checklist for better organization:

  - Include the current state, expected/observed behavior, and steps to reproduce the issue (recommended):

    - [] Describe the current state, including relevant details and prerequisites.
    - [] Describe the expected behavior and observed issue with the affected module or product.
    - [] If applicable, provide steps to reproduce the issue.

    Alternatively, if some of these items are not applicable, you may have already encountered the issue in the project. Proceed to the next step.

  - Skip the repro steps if you have already encountered the issue in the project (recommended):

    - [] Describe the current state to identify the problem.
    - [] Mark as a duplicate of [closed similar issue's ticket ID if already reported]
    - [] Observe: Issue

    Alternatively, if you are certain that you are the first one encountering the issue, continue with the following:

    *Template for Original Reporting of the Issue*

    - [] Describe the current state to identify the problem.
    - [] Estimate: This issue has likely not been encountered before, but if you disagree, you may mark this as a duplicate of [closed similar issue's ticket ID if already reported].

- If applicable, provide any additional context about the problem, such as setup, environments, or risks.

6. Expected Result

Clearly state what you expect the result should be, assuming your description in step 5 above is not the desired behavior.

7. Priority

Assign a priority to the issue based on its potential impact on your project or product. Priorities are project-specific but here are some examples:

- **High:** If the issue impacts project functionality or causes a delay in completing project milestones.
- **Medium:** If the issue impacts performance, usability or affects business processes to a lesser extent.
- **Low:** If the issue is minor, does not affect functionality or is not a significant performance or usability issue.

8. Additional Information (Optional)

If appropriate, you may add further details to the ticket to provide a more comprehensive understanding for the developers or relevant stakeholders. Here are some examples:

- [] Reference any relevant bug reports, discussions, or similar issues.
- [] Include screenshots or screenshots galleries to illustrate the issue.
- [] Specify the JIRA version, plugin version, or any other project-specific information as necessary.
- [] Add any other information that may be helpful in understanding the issue.

Submission

Once you have confirmed the accuracy and completeness of the above details, you can submit your JIRA ticket. To do this, follow the instructions listed in your JIRA project for creating a new issue. If you're not sure where to find this, refer to your JIRA project's documentation for creating new tickets. 

Note: If you use the JIRA Service Desk app, you can customize this template as per your customer view and add JSD templates to allow customers to create tickets related to your project. Check out the JSD documentation for more information.

Im Rahmen der Softwareentwicklung beschreiben User Stories, was der Benutzer vom System erwartet, während Akzeptanzkriterien die Bedingungen beschreiben, die eine bestimmte User Story erfüllen muss. Erstellen Sie grundlegende Akzeptanzkriterien basierend auf der gegebenen User Story.

User Story: Als Benutzer möchte ich in ein Suchfeld eine Stadt, einen Namen oder eine Straße eingeben, um passende Hoteloptionen zu finden.
output_1:
### Akzeptanzkriterien für die User Story:

1. **Suchfeld Verfügbarkeit:**
   - Das System muss ein Suchfeld auf der Hauptseite bereitstellen.
   - Das Suchfeld sollte leicht erkennbar und zugänglich sein.

2. **Eingabeakzeptanz:**
   - Das Suchfeld muss die Eingabe von Text erlauben, einschließlich Städtenamen, Personennamen oder Straßennamen.
   - Das Suchfeld sollte eine Mindestanzahl von Zeichen erfordern, bevor eine Suche initiiert wird (z.B. mindestens 3 Zeichen).

3. **Autovervollständigung:**
   - Während der Eingabe sollten Vorschläge (Autovervollständigung) angezeigt werden, basierend auf den bisher eingegebenen Zeichen.
   - Die Vorschläge sollten relevante Städte, Namen oder Straßen enthalten.

4. **Suchergebnisse:**
   - Nach der Eingabe und Bestätigung (z.B. durch Drücken der Enter-Taste oder Klicken auf ein Suchsymbol) sollte das System eine Liste von Hotels anzeigen, die den Suchkriterien entsprechen.
   - Die Ergebnisse sollten Informationen wie Hotelname, Adresse, Bewertung und Preis enthalten.

5. **Leistung und Antwortzeit:**
   - Die Suchergebnisse sollten innerhalb von maximal 5 Sekunden nach der Suchanfrage angezeigt werden.
   - Die Autovervollständigungsvorschläge sollten innerhalb von maximal 2 Sekunden erscheinen.

6. **Fehlerbehandlung:**
   - Bei Eingabe eines nicht erkennbaren oder nicht existierenden Namens oder Ortes sollte eine angemessene Fehlermeldung angezeigt werden (z.B. "Keine Ergebnisse gefunden. Bitte überprüfen Sie Ihre Eingabe.").
   - Das System sollte robust gegenüber Fehleingaben sein (z.B. Sonderzeichen oder Zahlen in Namen).

7. **Benutzerfreundlichkeit und Zugänglichkeit:**
   - Das Suchfeld und die Ergebnisse sollten auch auf mobilen Geräten gut lesbar und leicht bedienbar sein.
   - Die Webseite sollte barrierefrei sein, um auch Nutzern mit Einschränkungen die Verwendung zu ermöglichen.

8. **Datenschutz und Sicherheit:**
   - Alle Suchanfragen sollten gemäß den Datenschutzrichtlinien behandelt werden.
   - Die Übertragung der Suchanfragen sollte sicher erfolgen (z.B. über HTTPS).

Diese Akzeptanzkriterien sollen sicherstellen, dass die Funktionalität des Suchfeldes den Erwartungen des Benutzers entspricht und eine effiziente, benutzerfreundliche und sichere Erfahrung bietet.
output_2:
Based on the provided User Story, here are some sample Acceptance Criteria that define fundamental conditions that a system should meet based on this user story:

1. Search Feature Existence:
As a user, it is essential to have a search feature in place to enable you to search for hotels based on location entities. The following acceptance criteria could be defined:

Acceptance Criteria:

a. The hotel system should have a search feature readily available for users to use when looking for hotels based on location information.
   - [Example] If the hotel system is a web application, there should be a search bar or a search field readily available within the web pages for users to enter their search terms. If it is a mobile application, there should be a search function or button within the app for users to access.

b. (Alternative for a different deployment scenario) Alternatively, if developing against a software library or API, ensure the library or API includes a search feature that can enable you to implement searching for hotels by location in your application.

2. Location-Based Search:
With a search feature in place, you can use the following acceptance criteria to define the functionality of a location-based search:

Acceptance Criteria:

a. The user should be able to input a valid location.
   - [Example] The system should allow users to enter any of the following pieces of information to locate hotels:
     -- City name (if applicable) - e.g., "New York"
     -- Specific address (if applicable) - e.g., "123 Broadway"
     -- Coordinates of the location (if applicable) - e.g., "40.674184, -74.006806"

   - (Alternative for a system with limited scope or assumptions made during initial requirements) If the location-based information falls under any of the following categories, the system should support the entry of these:

     -- Location types that the system supports (e.g., city, state, country, etc.)
     -- Maximum number of location entries that can be specified (if applicable, e.g. One city, multiple cities)
     -- Accepted formats or input templates for location (if applicable, e.g. "City, State", partial geocodes, etc.)

b. The system should return search results that are located at the specified location.
   - [Example] When users enter a valid location and execute a search, the hotel system should return an aggregated list of hotel options located in, or near, the specified location.

3. Search for Hotels by Location:
To enable users to find hotel options based on location, the following acceptance criteria can be defined:

Acceptance Criteria:

a. The user should be able to search for one or more of the following location-based hotel information:

   - Hotel name - if searching for a specific hotel, the system should be able to return relevant results based on the user-provided name.
   - Lodging options - rather than searching for a specific hotel, users may want to browse a list or directory containing multiple hotels available at the specified location.
   - Room with unique name - instead of searching for hotels by name, some users may want to search for a specific room within an already-known hotel, which can also be validated and returned as a result.

b. The system should be able to provide search results for hotel options based on the user's search query.
   - [Example] When the user enters a search term in the provided search field (along with location information, as specified in the previous criterion), the hotel system should take the input and return a list of hotel options that match the search criteria.

c. Search results relevance - search results should be sorted and ordered based on the relevance of the matched results to the search query. The relevance of the search result can be based on keywords, filters, or any other search parameters.

   - [Example] The search results should be prioritized and ordered to put the most relevant hotel options at the top of the list, based on the search criteria provided by the user. For instance, the most relevant result should appear first if the user searched for a hotel with all the search terms entered, while a hotel listing that matches fewer criteria should be ranked lower in the search results.

   - (Alternative) The hotel API should return a list of matched hotels sorted by their relevance to the search query, with the highest matching hotel appearing first in the list, with optional support for pagination or infinite scrolling.

4. Search for Hotels by Location (Advanced):
If the user requires more specific search functionality, the following criteria can be defined:

Acceptance Criteria:

a. Search results filtering - the user should have the ability to filter search results based on specific criteria.

   - [Example] Users can filter search results based on additional search criteria, such as:

     -- Hotel star rating
     -- Number of stars
     -- Property type (e.g. Hotel, apartment, villa, etc.)
     -- Room type
     -- Number of rooms
     -- Check-in date
     -- Check-out date (e.g., the system should be able to filter out hotels that have already been checked out at the time of the search)
     -- Amenities (e.g., pool, gym, free Wi-Fi, etc.)
     -- Price range (e.g., minimum and/or maximum nightly cost)

   - (Alternative) The hotel API should support the following input parameters:

     -- Check-in date
     -- Room type
     -- Amenities (as array)
     -- Price range (in currency, minimum and maximum prices for a room)

b. Multiple search criteria - users should be able to apply multiple search criteria to narrow down their search results.

   - [Example] Users can apply multiple filters to their search to refine the results, such as:

     -- Hotel name (or ID)
     -- Check-in date (or from)
     -- Check-out date (or to)
     -- Room type
     -- Amenities (with at least one selected)
     -- Price range (minimum and maximum)

   - (Alternative) The hotel search feature should allow users to apply multiple search criteria, such as:

     -- q (optional with or without) - include a query string for searching hotel name or other identifiable attributes.
     -- check-in date range (specified by min and max values)
     -- check-out date range (specified by min and max values)
     -- room type (specified as a specific type)
     -- amenities (specified as an array of enabled amenities)
     -- price range (specified as a range between min and max values)

5. Localization:
To support multiple languages, the following acceptance criteria can be defined:

Acceptance Criteria:

a. Results localization - the hotel system should be able to display the search results in a language that corresponds to a selected locale.

   - [Example] When the user has selected a particular locale, the hotel names and other hotel-related strings (e.g., room descriptions, amenities) in the search results will be translated to the corresponding language.

   - (Alternative) The hotel API should support localization by returning results in the desired language, with translations for each supported language.

b. Search query localization - users should be able to search in their preferred language.

   - [Example] Users can select their preferred language and enter search terms in that language to get results that are translated to the same language. If no language is specified, the system should support a default language.

   - (Alternative) The hotel search feature should allow users to input search terms in a desired language option (such as location, address, or hotel name in string format), and the search results will be in the same language. The system should support localization for search criteria in one of the supported languages.
